title: Up to 50% off Subscriptions ($74.99 Annual Premium) @ iQIYI
body:
Deal: Up to 50% off Subscriptions ($74.99 Annual Premium) @ iQIYI

[micro78] I've read this description twice now, and still have no clue what an iqiyi is.
[skinnybutt1] It's a Chinese streaming platform like Netflix but worse, and it makes you see ads too.
[SBOB] streaming platform like Netflix but worse, and it makes you see ads too.
Right….so it's like 2026 Netflix?
[zbzylg] I would wake up in great delight every single day if iqiyi has any comparability.
[cerealsmok3r] asian streaming platform. think they do movies as well as all the c/j/k dramas
[h3blade] they have VIP and svip and ssvip and sssvip and ultimate VIP 1 to 1000 to eligible different ADs
true stories
[0806449] Don't buy…
That's supposedly unlucky number.
[Benoffie] Yes you can. That's thankfully explained well in the link so uou can stack with the $1.99 first month intro offer too
[Benoffie] Depends on level. Click the link for a comparison guide but I believe Premium is 4, Standard is 1
[CodeXD] Is iQIYI content on torbox? I remember trying to find a few when I was on RD and couldn't find them.
[belongsinforums] Need to get on Chinese internet. Baidu cloud used to have a lot. Now it's not so open
[mookill] Any good alternatives?
I would love to watch some asian dramas and movies that arent in western platforms
[Benoffie] I habe Viki and there are some overlaps especially with CDramas.
But Viki never comes on sale, they are really enforcing the 720p limits on the Standard now and they can be slow to release vs iQ which will release quicker. At 50% off, iQ Premium is the same price as Viki Standard so if you really like CDramas, hit that first.
There is also Kocowa+ - Viki's deal with them seems to be in flux atm. Mainly KDramas. Premium is $130pa. No real sales. They do free trials and upgrade to annual, get 2 months free type deals
[mookill] Thank you, how long have you used viki for?
[Benoffie] This'll be my 3rd? Year of addiction 🙄🤣
Right now watching Lament of Autumn while waiting for Make Me Tingle next week (unfortunately KDramas coming off live TV releases don't release quicker online. They go live in Korea then hit streaming services usually within 24 hours)
Also - ratings and reviews on Viki make no sense. Everything is either 1 or 10. If, like me, you try and be reasonable or critical, watch out. Full of fans. Look to Rotten Tomatoes 🍅 and IMDB if ratings matter to you.
Subtitles are excellent though. Great volunteers.
[neverpayfullretail] There's also Viu available in Australia now. But I find there's a lot of overlap with Viki and Kocowa. But you might find some content there you're interested in (just with ads). I would start there and then if you're really hitting a wall with paid content check out Viki or Kocowa.
[frankfu1122] Does anyone know if this blocks access when traveling outside of Australia?
[neverpayfullretail] Not so far as I'm aware. The only services I've found that have regional blocks (due to licensing agreements in different countries) are Viki, sometimes Kocowa and Viu. If you have used all 3 it probably means it's on a different platform in another country. Mostly found the licensing swaps in SE Asia. So in Malaysia I might see a drama I was watching in Singapore on Viki now only on ViU etc. YMMV with VPNs in those cases.
